Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old with acute shortness of breath, pleuritic right-sided back pain, subjective fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis beginning today; on methotrexate for SLE; remote exam reassuring; plan for same-day in-person evaluation to assess for pneumonia vs other causes; no prescriptions given.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute breathlessness with pain on deep inspiration localized to right posterior chest/back; coughed up blood twice today.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms started today; patient felt generally fine yesterday.
- Associated symptoms: Subjective fever (no thermometer used); awareness of heartbeat (no measured tachycardia on remote check); cough with blood.
- Functional impact: 2 weeks of increased fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and more difficulty with daily activities.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Pain worse on deep breaths (pleuritic). No reported relieving factors.
- Pertinent negatives noted by clinician inquiry: No recent long-haul flights; no personal or family history of blood clots.
- Cancer concern: Patient worried about lung cancer; clinician explained current presentation is more consistent with acute infection and not typical for lung cancer.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) — on methotrexate; no other comorbid diagnoses reported.

Medications:
- Methotrexate (for SLE); dose/route/frequency not documented. Last taken: this morning.
- Allergies: Denies medication and other allergies.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Occupation: Office/desk job.
- Living situation: Lives alone in a flat.
- Pets: Cat.
- Travel/immobilization: Denies recent long-haul flights.

Family History:
- Denies family history of venous thromboembolism.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Remote pulse check by patient count ~66–74 bpm, regular. Temperature, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation not recorded.
- General: Appears not acutely unstable per clinician’s impression via video.
- HEENT: Oropharynx visualized, normal appearance.
- Lymph: No enlarged cervical nodes on patient self-palpation.
- Perfusion: Capillary refill appeared normal on video.
- Respiratory: No in-person chest auscultation performed (video visit).
- Remainder of exam: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None obtained during this video visit.
- Plan: Same-day face-to-face visit for chest auscultation and full set of vitals (BP, HR, temperature). Antibiotics may be started if pneumonia suspected. Possible follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms do not settle, per clinician.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute pleuritic respiratory symptoms with minor hemoptysis in an SLE patient on methotrexate. Working diagnosis: community-acquired chest infection/pneumonia; requires same-day in-person assessment. Other considerations include pulmonary embolism and acute bronchitis.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  1) Community-acquired pneumonia with pleurisy: Supported by subjective fever, pleuritic right-sided pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and immunosuppression (methotrexate); opposed by lack of objective fever and no focal lung exam yet.
  2) Pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction: Supported by triad of pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis and SLE-associated VTE risk; opposed by normal pulse on remote check, subjective fever suggesting infection, and no recent travel or VTE history.
  3) Acute bronchitis: Possible with acute cough, fever, minor hemoptysis; opposed by focal pleuritic pain and immunosuppression favoring pneumonia.

- Issue 1: Acute dyspnea, pleuritic right-sided back pain, and hemoptysis — suspected chest infection/pneumonia.
  - Plan:
    - Same-day face-to-face clinic review arranged.
    - Perform vitals (BP, HR, temperature, and ideally oxygen saturation) and chest auscultation.
    - Start antibiotics if findings consistent with pneumonia (allergy status: none reported).
    - No prescriptions issued now pending in-person assessment.
    - Consider follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms do not settle, per clinician.

- Issue 2: Pulmonary embolism (rule-out consideration).
  - Plan:
    - Assess in person; if clinical suspicion persists after exam, proceed per clinic protocol for further workup (e.g., D-dimer/imaging) as indicated.

- Issue 3: Health anxiety regarding lung cancer.
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided: acute 1-day febrile pleuritic presentation with minor hemoptysis is not typical for lung cancer.
    - Reevaluate after in-person exam; consider imaging if symptoms persist or exam suggests alternative pathology (clinician mentioned possible chest X-ray if not improving).

- General plan items:
  - Support team contact provided to arrange the same-day face-to-face appointment.
  - Return earlier for any deterioration (increasing breathlessness, chest pain, high fever, persistent or heavy hemoptysis, confusion) — [note: general safety-netting implied; explicit phrasing not documented].

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Objective temperature, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and lung auscultation not obtained during video visit; no chest imaging or labs available; methotrexate dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Conflicts between sources: Patient identifiers conflict noted in transcript (name initially given as “Tracy Chapman”; later patient states name as “Doris”) — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Video exam limited; otherwise history understandable.
